**Refuting evidence for this task's INTERMITTENT / flake-hardening frame — the node is DETERMINISTIC per launch context, and the fix that follows is different.**

Source: task #2176 round 1 (2026-08-07). Its layer-(b) diff touches
`.claude/rules/code-style.md`, which selected this node into the gate-matched set;
the implementer reported the red and root-caused it, and the #2176 orchestrator
then verified the attribution independently. That verification produced three
measurements this task's body does not have.

## Measurements

1. **The reparent target is the nearest registered child subreaper, and under a
   Claude Code session that is always `systemd --user`.** Ancestry walk from a
   pytest-launching shell in this session:
   `bash(2507138) → claude(1048356) → node(1048276) → node(201205) →
   systemd(2887) → 1`. A setsid orphan therefore reparents to **2887**, never to
   pid 1, for any test run from inside a Claude Code session. This is the
   mechanism, stated as a property of the ancestry rather than as an observation.

2. **The subreaper has been up 138 days, so its presence cannot explain
   intermittency.** `ps -o pid,lstart,etime -p 2887` → started
   `Sat Mar 21 13:47:08 2026`, elapsed `138-20:20:44`. It was therefore equally
   present at this task body's cited **green** run (2026-08-06T06:40Z). The
   green/red split is NOT "sometimes a subreaper exists".

3. **Two consecutive re-runs both FAIL, in the same context.**
   `uv run pytest tests/test_workflow_setsid_detach_convention.py::test_setsid_child_survives_group_kill -q`
   at the repo root on clean `main`, run twice back to back → FAILED, FAILED. The
   failure is `assert _ppid(detached_pid) == "1"` →
   `AssertionError: assert '2887' == '1'`.

## What this changes

This task body concludes: "Red at ~15:44Z and ~19:35–19:50Z, green at 06:40Z with
the file untouched ⇒ the node is INTERMITTENT, not persistently red — the correct
frame is flake-hardening, not 'fix the red node'." Measurements 2 and 3 refute
that inference. The node is deterministic **given the launch context**: it fails
whenever the runner's ancestry passes through a registered child subreaper, and
passes when it does not (a cron job, a systemd *system*-scope service, or a shell
parented outside the user manager). The 06:40Z green run is explained by a
different launch context, not by a different roll of the dice.

**The practical consequence is that the fix differs.** Under the flake frame the
natural remedy is retry/tolerance hardening, which would never help — every retry
inside a Claude Code session reparents to 2887 again. The correct remedy is the
one #2176's implementer proposed: the assertion is over-specific, so accept pid 1
**OR** a subreaper.

Note the guarded property itself HELD in every run: the two assertions preceding
the failure both pass ("plain nohup child survived the group kill" and "setsid
child died with the group kill" both hold), i.e. the setsid child does survive the
group kill and does escape the dead session's ppid tree. Only the literal `== "1"`
is wrong. The test's own inline comment ("the setsid child reparented to PID 1")
encodes the same incorrect assumption and should be corrected alongside the
assert.

Suggested assertion, unchanged in intent from this task's existing
`proposed_fix`: assert the detached pid's parent is no longer the (dead) wrapper
and lies outside the wrapper's session — e.g. `_ppid(detached_pid) !=
str(wrapper.pid)` plus either `_ppid(...) == "1"` or
`/proc/<ppid>/comm == "systemd"`. That passes in both launch contexts and still
fails if the child is genuinely killed or left parented to the wrapper.

**Archiving as a duplicate of #2199, which fixed this exact assertion.**

Both tasks target the same line of the same file:
`tests/test_workflow_setsid_detach_convention.py::test_setsid_child_survives_group_kill`,
`assert _ppid(detached_pid) == "1"`. #2199 was the task invoked and carried the
stronger evidence base (deterministic repro, exact line, ranked fix options with
an explicit do-NOT guard), so the fix executed there. Nothing from this task was
dropped — all three of its unique contributions were folded into #2199's plan:

1. The 2026-08-05 #1996 sighting history (the ~15:44Z standalone park and the
   ~19:35–19:50Z Step 10d pre-push both-trees park, fp `4516c07c1164`).
2. The green-at-2026-08-06T06:40Z datapoint, which is what pinned the failure as
   CONTEXT-dependent rather than load-flaky.
3. This body's acceptance bar — *"the node is reliably green on pristine main in
   every execution context"* — which became #2199 plan criterion 5 and is a
   strictly better deliverable statement than #2199's own.

**This task's `unverified hypothesis — verify at plan time` is now CLOSED, and it
was right.** The hypothesis read: *"the subreaper reparenting above is
miner-inferred from the assertion diff, not probed against the live process
tree."* Probed at #2199 plan time: `ps -p 2887 -o pid=,ppid=,comm=` →
`2887 1 systemd`, and 2887 is a genuine ancestor of the pytest process — the
per-user `systemd` instance, a `PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER` process. The inference
was correct.

**One correction to this body's framing, for the record.** This task concluded
*"the node is INTERMITTENT, not persistently red — the correct frame is
flake-hardening, not 'fix the red node'"*, while #2199 framed it as persistent.
Both observations were sound; both general claims were wrong. The failure is
**deterministic given the process ancestry** and **context-dependent across
ancestries**: red wherever a subreaper ancestor exists (every Happy/Claude
session, which descends from `systemd --user`), green in an ancestry that adopts
straight to the pid-namespace init — which is what this task's own compose-time
cron run was, exactly as it hypothesised. It is not load-flaky: the #2199 repro
ran in isolation, one file, 0.46 s. That distinction mattered for the fix — a
timing/retry hardening, which "flake-hardening" implies, would have been the
wrong instrument and would not have made the node green.

The landed fix replaces the literal with membership in the set the kernel may
legitimately adopt into (`{pytest} ∪ ancestors(pytest) ∪ {1}`, per
`find_new_reaper`) plus an assert that the target is not the dead launcher, and
adds a committed case pinning that the set rejects a live descendant so the
membership assert cannot go vacuous. This satisfies this task's own § Proposed
change ("accept reparenting to ANY pid outside the killed process group... the
invariant under test is not 'init adopts it'") without loosening the case to a
bare liveness check.
